ITQAN:v2p498/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p498/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p498/r2.claim: One analysis calls the lām a particle of consequence: enmity was the outcome, not the captors' purpose; some call this figurative causation.

ITQAN:v2p498/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p498/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v2p498/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a literal purposive reading, supplying an omitted noun: they took Moses for fear he would become an enemy.
ITQAN:v2p498/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان الذي عندي أنها للتعليل حقيقة

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r12.claim: The Pharaoh-family phrase فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا is cited as another example of a consequential lām.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r12.anchor: نحو قوله: (فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p525/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p525/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p525/r5.claim: Context implies that when danger approached, Moses’ mother put him in a papyrus box and consigned it to the Nile; the Torah describes her hiding him before doing so.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p525/r5.anchor: God directed her to place Moses (sws) in a box

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r1.claim: The Nile carried the box from Israelite settlements toward Pharaoh’s palace, where royal family members found the beautiful infant and brought him inside.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r1.anchor: The river Nile, passing through various settlements of the Israelites, flowed towards the palace of the Pharaoh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s kind-hearted wife urged him not to kill the child, suggesting he might benefit them or be adopted; the author relates her kindness to 66:11.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r2.anchor: the boy should not be killed for he may be of benefit to them or they may adopt him as their son

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r3.claim: The word آل indicates that the whole royal household, young and old, went to the box and carried Moses to the palace.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r3.anchor: all of them carried him back to the palace

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r4.claim: The lām expresses consequence: the family picked Moses up hoping for comfort, unaware that he would end Pharaoh’s supremacy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r4.anchor: the supremacy and power of the Pharaoh will be routed forever

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r5.claim: The comment that Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies did not know the outcome rebukes their belief that their power would let them continue oppressing Israel; God raised their enemy in their palace.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p526/r5.anchor: their greatest enemy be raised in their royal palace through the king and the queen

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r12.claim: An omitted sequence says she nursed Moses and cast him into the river; li-yakuna describes the eventual consequence of Pharaoh's family taking him, although they intended adoption and affection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r12.anchor: واللام في ليكون للتعليل المجازي، لما كان مآل التقاطه وتربيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r13.claim: Most read huznan with both vowels open, a Quraysh dialect; several named readers use a damma on ha and sukun on za.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وحزنا، بفتح الحاء والزاي، وهي لغة قريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r14.claim: A khatiʾ commits error deliberately, unlike a mukhtiʾ; the likely omitted sense is that Moses became their enemy and grief because they persisted in crimes and unbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p286#2/r14.anchor: والخاطئ: المتعمد الخطأ، والمخطئ: الذي لا يتعمده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r1.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Pharaoh's family wronged themselves by taking Moses; other explanations blame killing Israelite children or raising their enemy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r1.anchor: خاطئين على أنفسهم بالتقاطه. وقيل: بقتل أولاد بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r2.claim: Pharaoh and Haman are both associated with the troops although Haman had none, since army maintenance requires the minister to raise funds and the king to command and compel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r2.anchor: إذ بالوزير تحصل الأموال، وبالملك وقهره يتوصل إلى تحصيلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p287/r3.claim: A reading without hamza in خاطئين may reflect deleted hamza, which is likeliest, or derive from خطا يخطو, missing the right course.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r1.claim: Iltiqāṭ means finding or picking something up without having sought it; the family of Pharaoh here means his female servants.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r1.anchor: فالالتقاط إصابة الشيء من غير طلب

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r2.claim: The commonly held view takes the lām as one of consequence; a purpose reading would conflict with Pharaoh’s wife calling Moses a comfort and God’s saying He cast love on him, as in 7:179.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r2.anchor: المشهور أن هذه اللام يراد بها العاقبة

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r3.claim: Rāzī prefers al-Zamakhsharī’s account: this is figurative purpose, since an object’s eventual outcome is treated as its aim, like calling a brave person a lion.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r3.anchor: هذه اللام هي لام التعليل على سبيل المجاز

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r4.claim: The poem “They bear children for death and build for ruin” illustrates a purpose construction whose result is the opposite of the apparent intent.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r4.anchor: وقوله الشاعر : لدوا للموت وابنوا للخراب

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r5.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ḥuznan with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy; the others read ḥazanan with fatḥa on both, two dialect forms like saqm and saqam.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ( حزنا ) بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says khāṭiʾīn here does not mean sinning: they did not realize this child would take their kingdom.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r6.anchor: قال الحسن معنى { كانوا خاطئين } ليس من الخطيئة

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r7.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r7.claim: Most exegetes understand that Pharaoh’s people were wrong in disbelief and oppression, so God made them raise their enemy, the cause of their destruction, themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r7.anchor: وأما جمهور المفسرين فقالوا معناه كانوا خاطئين فيما كانوا عليه من الكفر والظلم

RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r8.claim: A shortened reading, khāṭīn, lightens khāṭiʾīn and means those who miss the right and go toward error.
RAZI-FULL:v24p195/r8.anchor: تخفيف خاطئين أي خاطين الصواب إلى الخطأ

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r1.claim: The opening fa links to an omitted preceding clause; iltiqāṭ is finding and picking something up without seeking it.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r1.anchor: {فالتقطه ءال فرعون} الفاء فصيحة مفصحة عن عطفه على جملة محذوفة والالتقاط إصابة الشيء من غير طلب

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r2.claim: A luqaṭa is unguarded property whose owner must be sought; a laqīṭ is a child of unknown lineage abandoned from poverty or fear of illicit birth.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r2.anchor: ومنه اللقطة وهو مال بلا حافظ ثم يعرف مالكه واللقيط هو طفل لم يعرف نسبه يطرح في الطريق

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r3.claim: It is obligatory to rescue an abandoned child if the child risks perishing, such as in water or before a predator; jurisprudence details the rule.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r3.anchor: ويجب رفعه إن خيف هلاكه بأن وجده في الماء أو بين يدي سبع وتفصيله في الفقه

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r4.claim: A man’s āl are his close adherents, whose affairs revert to him through kinship, companionship, or religious agreement.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r4.anchor: وآل الرجل خاصته الذين يؤول إليه أمرهم للقراءة أو الصحبة أو الموافقة في الدين.

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r5.claim: After Moses’ mother put him in a chest as commanded and cast it into the river, Pharaoh’s people picked him up carefully and protected him from loss.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r5.anchor: والمعنى فألقته في اليم بعد ما جعلته في التابوت حسبما أمرت به فالتقطه آل فرعون أي أخذوه أخذ اعتناء به وصيانة له عن الضياع.

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r6.claim: The lām signals consequence, not purpose: Pharaoh’s household did not take Moses in order to make him their enemy and grief.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r6.anchor: {ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا} اللام لام العاقبة والصيرورة لا لام العلة والإرادة لأنهم لم يلتقطوه

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r7.claim: The outcome is presented like the purpose because it followed their motive of love and adoption; calling Moses ‘grief’ himself intensifies their sorrow.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r7.anchor: ولكن صار عاقبة أمرهم إلى ذلك أبرز مدخولها في معرض العلة لالتقاطهم تشبيها له في الترتب عليه بالغرض الحامل عليه

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r8.claim: Al-Kashifi explains Moses as enemy to men drowned through Pharaoh’s cruelty and grief to women whose sons were enslaved.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r8.anchor: قال الكاشفي : {عدوا} (دشمني مر مردانرا كه بسبب فرعون غرق شوند {وحزنا} واندوهي بزرك مرزنانرا

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r9.claim: The trio were wrong in all their actions, so it was unsurprising they killed thousands and then raised the child whose coming they feared.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r9.anchor: في كل ما يأتون وما يذرون فليس ببدع منهم أن قتلوا ألوفا لأجله ثم أخذوه يربونه

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r10.claim: Khaṭiʾa denotes knowingly straying into error, a fully culpable act; akhṭaʾ is an unintentional mistake against one’s intent.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r10.anchor: والخاطىء من يأتي بالخطأ وهو يعلم أنه خطأ وهو الخطأ التام المأخوذ به الإنسان

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r11.claim: The unintentional person means to do what is good but slips and does something contrary to that intention.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r11.anchor: والمخطىء من يأتي به وهو لا يعلم أي يريد ما يحسن فعله ولكن يقع منه بخلاف ما يريد

BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r12.claim: A report says Pharaoh’s daughter put Moses’ saliva on her leprosy and was cured at once.
BURSEVI:v6p278#3/r12.anchor: حكي : أنهم فتحوا التابوت ورأوا موسى ألقى الله محبته في قلوب القوم وعمدت ابنة فرعون إلى ريقه

STUDYQURAN:28:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r1.claim: The baby’s becoming their enemy and sorrow was not the rescuers’ intention but the eventual outcome God had in store for them.
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r1.anchor: does not mean that this was the intention of those from the House of Pharaoh who took the baby

STUDYQURAN:28:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r2.claim: Khāṭiʾ can mean sinners or people who make a mistake.
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r2.anchor: Sinners translates khāṭiʾ, which can also mean those who make a mistake

STUDYQURAN:28:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r3.speaker: a minority of commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r3.claim: A minority reads the hosts as mistaken about the situation rather than sinful.
STUDYQURAN:28:8/r3.anchor: for a minority of commentators their hosts were sinners

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains iltiqāṭ as an unexpected meeting or finding, without seeking the thing beforehand.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r1.anchor: أصبته التقاطا، ولقيت فلانا التقاطا؛ ومنه قول الراجز

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r2.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r2.claim: An anonymous rajaz verse uses iltiqāṭ to describe unexpectedly reaching a watering place, witnessing the sense of sudden encounter.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r2.anchor: ومنهل وردته التقاطا … لم ألق إذ وردته فراطا

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says Asiya's maidservants found the chest among trees near Pharaoh's house, brought it to her thinking it held treasure, and she loved the baby and persuaded Pharaoh not to kill him despite his fear that Moses was an Israelite child who would destroy them.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " أقبل الموج بالتابوت يرفعه مرة ويخفضه أخرى، حتى أدخله بين أشجار عند بيت فرعون، فخرج جواري آسية امرأة فرعون

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r4.speaker: محمد بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r4.claim: Muḥammad ibn Qays says Pharaoh's daughter, who was afflicted with leprosy, found the chest; looking at Moses cured her, and she declared him blessed and pleaded for his life.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس، قال: " كانت بنت فرعون برصاء، فجاءت إلى النيل، فإذا التابوت في النيل تخفقه الأمواج، فأخذته بنت فرعون، فلما فتحت التابوت

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Pharaoh's agents retrieved the chest after Asiya spotted it in the Nile; when they found the baby, God's love for him entered Pharaoh's heart and Asiya asked that they not kill him.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " أصبح فرعون في مجلس له كان يجلسه على شفير النيل كل غداة: فبينما هو جالس

TAB-FULL:v18p159/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī does not prefer one reported identification of Pharaoh's household over another; he retains the verse's general wording and refers back to his earlier explanation of āl.
TAB-FULL:v18p159/r6.anchor: ولا قول في ذلك عندنا أولى بالصواب مما قال الله عز وجل: {فالتقطه آل فرعون} [القصص: 8] وقد بينا معنى الآل فيما

TAB-FULL:v18p162/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r1.claim: The lām describes the eventual outcome, not the purpose for which Pharaoh's people took Moses: they thought he would benefit them, but his eventual role brought their destruction, as God had willed.
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r1.anchor: وليس لذلك أخذوه، ولكن امرأة فرعون قالت: {قرة عين لي ولك}

TAB-FULL:v18p162/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains that Moses became their enemy and grief in the final outcome of his affair, by God's will, although that was not why they took him.
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، في قوله: " {فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا} [القصص: 8] قال: ليكون في عاقبة أمره عدوا وحزنا لما أراد الله به

TAB-FULL:v18p162/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r3.claim: He compares the wording to rebuking someone whose apparently beneficial act ultimately harms him: they took Moses expecting comfort, but the outcome was their ruin at his hands.
TAB-FULL:v18p162/r3.anchor: وقد كان الفاعل في حال فعله ذلك عند نفسه يفعله راجيا نفعه، غير أن العاقبة جاءت بخلاف ما كان يرجو

TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r1.claim: Qatādah glosses Moses as their enemy in religion and grief over what would befall them through him.
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا} [القصص: 8] عدوا لهم في دينهم، وحزنا لما يأتيهم

TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r2.speaker: قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r2.claim: Most Kufan readers read ḥuznan with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy.
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r2.anchor: وقرأته عامة قراء الكوفة: (وحزنا) بضم الحاء وتسكين الزاي.

TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r3.claim: With fatḥa, ḥazanan is the verbal noun of ḥazintu; with ḍamma and sukūn, ḥuzn is a noun, like the two forms al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm.
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r3.anchor: والحزن بفتح الحاء والزاي مصدر من حزنت حزنا، والحزن بضم الحاء وتسكين الزاي الاسم: كالعدم والعدم ونحوه.

TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī regards the two readings as close in meaning and both correct, like the variants al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm.
TAB-FULL:v18p162#2/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان متقاربتا المعنى، وهما على اختلاف اللفظ فيهما بمنزلة العدم، والعدم، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب.

TABATABAI:28:7-8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r6.claim: Iltqāṭ is finding and taking something without having sought it; al-yamm is the sea or a large river, and ilqāʾ is casting or throwing.
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r6.anchor: إصابة الشيء وأخذه من غير طلب، ومنه اللقطة

TABATABAI:28:7-8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r7.claim: An unnamed reported grammatical view takes the lām in “so that he would be an enemy and grief” as a lām of eventual outcome.
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r7.anchor: واللام في قوله { ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا } للعاقبة - على ما قيل -

TABATABAI:28:7-8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r8.claim: Grief denotes its cause, a figurative intensification of how strongly Moses would cause their grief; ḥazan and ḥuzn mean the same thing.
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r8.anchor: والمراد بالحزن سبب الحزن فإطلاق الحزن عليه مبالغة في سببيته لحزنهم.

TABATABAI:28:7-8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r9.claim: Khāṭiʾ describes someone who intends an act he does not do well and performs it; mukhṭiʾ describes someone who intends a fitting act but ends up doing something else.
TABATABAI:28:7-8/r9.anchor: والفرق بين الخاطئ والمخطئ على ما ذكره الراغب أن الخاطئ يطلق على من أراد فعلا لا يحسنه

TABRISI:28:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:8/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:8/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that the midwife loved and warned Moses’ mother; his sister hid him in a lit furnace God cooled; later a carpenter’s failed attempts to expose the mother signaled divine intervention.
TABRISI:28:8/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما قربت ولادة أم موسى

TABRISI:28:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:8/r2.claim: Al-taqāṭ means Pharaoh’s household found and took Moses without seeking him.
TABRISI:28:8/r2.anchor: أي أصابوه وأخذوه من غير طلب

TABRISI:28:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:8/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:8/r3.claim: The phrase describes the eventual outcome, not their purpose in taking Moses: a person may earn wealth that brings ruin without intending it.
TABRISI:28:8/r3.anchor: لا أنهم أخذوه لهذا كما يقال لمن كسب مالا فأداه ذلك إلى الحتف والهلاك

TABRISI:28:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:8/r4.claim: Pharaoh, Hāmān, and their troops disobeyed God in their actions.

TABRISI:28:8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:8/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:8/r5.claim: The Nile carried the chest to Pharaoh and his wife; Āsiya opened it and loved Moses. She was an Israelite of prophetic descent, compassionate and charitable to believers.
TABRISI:28:8/r5.anchor: وكانت آسية بنت مزاحم امرأة من بني إسرائيل استنكحها فرعون وهي من خيار النساء

THALABI:v7p235/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r1.claim: Pharaoh's only, beloved daughter had severe leprosy; doctors and magicians said a child found from the sea would heal her if his saliva were applied at a specified sunrise.
THALABI:v7p235/r1.anchor: فقالوا له: أيها الملك لا تبرأ إلا من قبل البحر يوجد منه شبه الإنسان

THALABI:v7p235/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r2.claim: On the appointed Monday, Pharaoh and Asiya sat by the Nile as the princess played at its bank; servants retrieved the chest, but could neither open nor break it.
THALABI:v7p235/r2.anchor: فلما كان يوم الاثنين غدا فرعون إلى مجلس كان له على شفير النيل ومعه آسية بنت مزاحم

THALABI:v7p235/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r3.claim: Asiya alone saw a light inside the chest and opened it; Moses lay in a cradle with light between his eyes, and God provided milk through his thumb.
THALABI:v7p235/r3.anchor: فإذا هي بصبي صغير في مهده،

THALABI:v7p235/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r4.claim: God placed love for Moses in Asiya's heart; Pharaoh also loved him, and the princess's application of his saliva cured her leprosy, so she embraced him.
THALABI:v7p235/r4.anchor: فألقى الله سبحانه لموسى (عليه السلام) المحبة في قلب آسية، وأحبه فرعون وعطف عليه،

THALABI:v7p235/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r5.claim: Pharaoh's advisers suspected Moses was the Israelite child feared by the regime and had been cast into the river to escape him; Pharaoh moved to kill the baby.
THALABI:v7p235/r5.anchor: فقال الغواة من قوم فرعون: أيها الملك إنا نظن إن ذلك المولود الذي نحذر منه من بني إسرائيل هو هذا،

THALABI:v7p235/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p235/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p235/r6.claim: Asiya pleaded that Moses might benefit them or be adopted as a son; she was childless and asked Pharaoh for him, so Pharaoh gave him to her while saying he himself had no need of the child.
THALABI:v7p235/r6.anchor: قالت آسية: قرت عين لي ولك، لا تقتله عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا، وكانت لا تلد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s household found Moses in the sea; the verb means coming upon an object without having sought it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r1.anchor: أي: من البحر، والالتقاط إصابة الشيء من غير طلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r2.claim: The people of Pharaoh here are his wife’s maidservants, who took Moses’ chest from the sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r2.anchor: والمراد بآل فرعون هاهنا: جواري امرأته اللاتي أخذن تابوت موسى من البحر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r3.claim: The two readings huznan and huzunan are dialectal variants, like the paired forms saqam and Arab.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r3.anchor: مثل السقم والسقم، والعرب والعرب، وبابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says the phrase describes the eventual outcome, not the family’s purpose in taking Moses; the cited verse likewise does not mean mothers give birth intending death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق:] (¬5) {ليكون لهم} أي: ليصير الأمر إلى ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r5.claim: Muqatil glosses the outcome as Moses becoming their enemy in their destruction and a source of grief in their hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: ليكون لهم عدوا في الهلاك، وغيظا في قلوبهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p336/r6.claim: The description means that Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies were disobedient sinners.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r3.claim: Pharaoh’s household took Moses from the water; the outcome was that he became their enemy and grief.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r3.anchor: { فالتقطه } أخذه { آل فرعون } عن الماء { ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا } أي: ليصير الأمر إلى ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r4.claim: Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops were disobedient and sinful.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:7-10/r4.anchor: إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين } أي: عاصين آثمين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r9.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r9.claim: Yaḥyā says the only report he heard was that washerwomen on the Nile picked Moses up.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r9.anchor: {فالتقطه آل فرعون} [القصص: 8] قال يحيى: لا أعلم إلا أنه بلغني أن الغسالات على النيل التقطته.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r10.claim: Qatāda explains that Moses opposed them in religion and brought them grief.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: {ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا} [القصص: 8] ، أي: ليكون لهم عدوا في دينهم وحزنا لهم يحزنهم به.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r11.claim: Pharaoh, Hāmān, and their troops were polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p578#2/r11.anchor: قال: {إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين} [القصص: 8] مشركين.

QASHANI:28:7-8/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:7-8/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:7-8/r4.claim: Pharaoh's family represents the dominant psychic faculties; discernment and protection require the aid of imagination, estimation, and the outer and inner senses.

QASHANI:28:7-8/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:7-8/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:7-8/r5.claim: Ultimately a person learns that his fiercest enemy is the self between his sides, then subdues its helpers by discipline and annihilates it through restraint, breaking, and mortification.
QASHANI:28:7-8/r5.anchor: في العاقبة ويعلم أن أعدى عدوه النفس التي بين جنبيه فيقهرها وأعوانها بالرياضة

ELMALILI:28:7-13/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:7-13/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:7-13/r6.claim: Khāṭiʾīn derives from khatīʾa, “sin,” rather than khaṭaʾ, “mistake”; the latter would take the form mukhṭiʾīn.

ELMALILI:28:7-13/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:7-13/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:7-13/r7.claim: Their being sinners explains why Moses would become their enemy and grief: God afflicted them in this way, and otherwise they would not have taken him in.
ELMALILI:28:7-13/r7.anchor: Bu âyet لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّۭا وَحَزَنًا hikmetinin vechini beyandır. Yani cânî oldukları için Allah tarafından o suretle mübtelâ olacaklardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r3.claim: As recompense for their persecution of Israel, Pharaoh’s family found the baby who would later become their enemy and cause of grief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r3.anchor: Firavun ailesi, İsrâiloğulları’na yapmış olduğu zulmün karşılığı olarak ileride kendilerine düşman ve üzüntü sebebi olacak bebeği Nil kıyısında bularak Firavun’a getirmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r4.claim: God surrounded Moses with love from Himself and placed love for him in people’s hearts so he could be protected, raised, and matured under divine care.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r4.anchor: Yüce Allah Mûsâ’nın korunup kollanması ve kendi gözetiminde yetiştirilip olgunlaşması için onu katından bir sevgi ile kuşatmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r5.claim: The love surrounding Moses is connected to God placing love for him in others’ hearts, as stated in Ta Ha.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r5.anchor: kezâ ona karşı insanların kalbine de sevgi yerleştirmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r6.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r6.claim: Razi identifies Pharaoh’s wife as Asiya; she pleaded to spare the child and keep him with her.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r6.anchor: Firavun’un eşi Asiye (Râzî, XXIV, 228), çocuğun hayatına kıyılmaması ve kendisinde kalması için Firavun’a ricada bulunmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r7.claim: Calling Moses the joy of both parents indicates delight; Pharaoh’s wife also suggested he might benefit them or be adopted, persuading her husband.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r7.anchor: “O, senin ve benim göz aydınlığımız, muradımız olsun!” diyerek bir sevinç ve mutluluk kaynağı olduğuna işaret ettikten sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r8.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r8.claim: The statement that they did not realize means Pharaoh and his men did not know what would later happen to them because of Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:7/r8.anchor: “Onlar işin farkında değillerdi” cümlesi Firavun ve adamlarının ileride Hz. Mûsâ sebebiyle başlarına gelecek olanları bilmediklerine işaret etmektedir (Razî, XXIV, 229)

BAQILLANI:v1p102/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p102/r1.claim: Bāqillānī defines tadhyīl as emphatic reinforcement, opposite to allusion, and gives the Pharaoh narrative through the Israelites' inheritance as a Quranic example.
BAQILLANI:v1p102/r1.anchor: وهو ضرب من التأكيد وهو ضد ما قدمنا ذكره من الإشارة

BURHAN:v3p91/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r4.claim: Although some take the lām as an unintended outcome, the source argues that divine acts carry wisdom though they are not compelled by it; an outcome lām applies to someone ignorant of consequences, not to God.
BURHAN:v3p91/r4.anchor: فالجواب أن معنى قولنا إن أفعال الله تعالى لا تعلل أي لا تجب ولكنها لا تخلو عن الحكمة

BURHAN:v3p91/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r5.claim: The lām is a lām of wisdom and intended purpose: the verse explains God’s decree and arrangement that they take him in; mentioning their action rather than the decree heightens their sorrow and regret.
BURHAN:v3p91/r5.anchor: وأما من هو بكل شيء عليم فمستحيله في حقه وإنما اللام الواردة في أحكامه وأفعاله لام الحكمة والغاية المطلوبة

BURHAN:v4p345/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p345/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p345/r1.claim: Lām can mark an outcome rather than an intended goal: Pharaoh's household took Moses up for the opposite reason, as their hope he might help them or be adopted shows.
BURHAN:v4p345/r1.anchor: وتسمى لام العاقبة فإن من المعلوم أنهم لم يلتقطوه لذلك بل لضده بدليل قوله

BURHAN:v4p345/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p345/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p345/r2.claim: Purpose lām can contain an understood kay; kay can occur with lām or without it, and the passage gives examples of both purpose and outcome.
BURHAN:v4p345/r2.anchor: ومثال لام كي وكي مضمرة معها قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p345/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p345/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BURHAN:v4p345/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba reports a proposed test for lām of consequence: it permits substituting fa in its place.
BURHAN:v4p345/r3.anchor: وحكى ابن قتيبة عن بعضهم إن علامتها جواز تقدير الفاء موضعها

BURHAN:v4p345/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p345/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p345/r5.claim: Zarkashi distinguishes purpose lām, whose result is the agent's aim, from consequence lām, which indicates only an outcome.
BURHAN:v4p345/r5.anchor: لكن الفرق بينها وبين لام التعليل التي في نحو قوله

BURHAN:v3p68#3/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr also counts the close about Pharaoh, Hāmān, and their troops as tadhyīl; Zarkashi allows that it may instead explain the preceding event.
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r8.anchor: ﴿ فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

BURHAN:v4p347/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p347/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p347/r1.claim: Zarkashi argues that the outcome reading still expresses causation: the pickup led to Moses' enmity, so the effect can ground a truthful causal statement even when unintended.
BURHAN:v4p347/r1.anchor: ما جعلوه للعاقبة هو راجع للتعليل فإن التقاطهم أفضى إلى عداوته وذلك يوجب صدق الإخبار بكون الالتقاط للعداوة

BURHAN:v4p347/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p347/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p347/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the lām causal metaphorically: their motive was love and adoption, while the result of taking Moses was likened to their motive.
BURHAN:v4p347/r2.anchor: التحقيق أنها لام العلة وأن التعليل بها وارد على طريق المجاز دون الحقيقة لأنه لم يكن داعيهم إلى الالتقاط كونه لهم عدوا وحزنا

BURHAN:v4p347/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p347/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
BURHAN:v4p347/r3.claim: Ibn Khālawayh reports that Kūfans call it lām of purpose, while Basrans call it lām of outcome, since they did not take Moses in order to make him their enemy.
BURHAN:v4p347/r3.anchor: وقال ابن خالويه في كتاب المبتدأ في النحو فأما قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p347/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p347/r4.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v4p347/r4.claim: Ibn al-Dahhān proposes an unusual reordered parsing in which عدوا وحزنا is a circumstantial description of the pronoun, meaning they took Moses to possess him.
BURHAN:v4p347/r4.anchor: وجوز ابن الدهان في الآية وجها غريبا على التقديم والتأخير

BURHAN:v4p347/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p347/r5.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v4p347/r5.claim: Ibn al-Dahhān also suggests that the pickup was motivated by aversion to Moses becoming their enemy and grief.
BURHAN:v4p347/r5.anchor: قال ويجوز إن يكون التقدير فالتقطه آل فرعون لكراهة إن يكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

SULAMI:v2p100#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p100#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p100#2/r1.claim: Sahl says Pharaoh’s household picked Moses up expecting joy, unaware that divine decree had hidden his becoming their enemy and grief.
SULAMI:v2p100#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : التقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم فرحا وسرورا ، ولم يعلموا ما اضمرت القدرة فيه من تصييره لهم عدوا وحزنا

ITQAN:v3p121/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p121/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p121/r9.claim: A derivative metaphor uses a non-generic form, including verbs and particles; here the lām is borrowed after comparing enmity and grief following the finding with an outcome implied by a goal.
ITQAN:v3p121/r9.anchor: وتبعية وهي ما كان اللفظ فيها غير اسم جنس كالفعل والمشتقات

ITQAN:v4p389/r32.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p389/r32.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p389/r32.claim: The person who picked Moses up was named Tabuth.
ITQAN:v4p389/r32.anchor: ﴿ فالتقطه آل فرعون ﴾ إسم الملتقط طابوث

TUSTARI:28:8/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:8/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:8/r1.claim: Pharaoh's household took Moses in expecting joy and delight, unaware that divine power had destined him to become their enemy and grief.
TUSTARI:28:8/r1.anchor: أي رفعوه ليكون لهم فرحا وسرورا ولم يعلموا، إنما أضمرت القدرة فيه

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r8.claim: Khāṭiʾūn can mean sinners guilty of shirk; the same applies to the people who do not eat from the tree in Hell.
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r8.anchor: يعني مذنبين في شرك وقال تعالى في سورة الحاقة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r4.claim: Khaṭaʾ can mean associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخطأ في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : - أحدها : الشرك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r1.claim: جنود is the plural of جند and denotes a large gathered number.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r1.anchor: الجنود : جمع جند : وهو العدد الكثير المجتمع .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r5.claim: A fourth sense is assembled multitudes, including Pharaoh, Haman and their troops.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الجنود في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p328#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p328#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p328#5/r1.claim: The family did not adopt Moses at that moment in order to make him an enemy; they took him as a son, and the concise wording says he later became their enemy and grief.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p328#5/r1.anchor: {فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا} لم يلتقطوه في وقتهم ذاك لهذه العلة. وإنما التقطوه: ليكون لهم ولدا بالتبني؛ فكان عدوا وحزنا فاختصر الكلام.

NAHHAS:v3p227/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p227/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p227/r11.claim: ليكون is accusative under the purpose lām; the construction is ordinary Arabic, even if weak grammarians object to it.
NAHHAS:v3p227/r11.anchor: نصب ليكون بلام كي وربما أشكل هذا على من يجهل اللغة

SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r1.claim: The lām may express figurative purpose, since the outcome is treated as the act’s motive, or result/consequence.
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r1.anchor: في اللام الوجهان المشهوران: العلية المجازية بمعنى: أن ذلك لما كان نتيجة فعلهم

SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r2.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r2.claim: The common reading has fatḥ on ḥāʾ and zāy; the two Hamza-and-Kisāʾī readings have ḍamma and sukūn, with both forms synonymous.
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r2.anchor: وقرأ العامة بفتح الحاء والزاي وهي لغة قريش والأخوان بضم وسكون

SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r3.claim: The common reading has hamza and derives from khaṭiʾa, error, the opposite of correctness.
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r3.anchor: العامة على الهمز. مأخوذ من الخطأ ضد الصواب

SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r4.claim: A hamza-less yāʾ reading may be the same word softened, or derive from khaṭā yakhtū, “to step past” what is correct.
SAMIN-DURR:28:8/r4.anchor: وقرىء بياء دون همزة، فاحتمل أن يكون كالأول ولكن خفف

ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r5.claim: The phrase is also read with the alternative vocalization حَزَنًا alongside حُزْنًا.

ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r6.claim: The clause describes an outcome, not their intention; it is like acquiring wealth that leads to one's death.
ZAJJAJ:v4p132/r6.anchor: ليصير الأمر إلى ذلك لا أنهم طلبوه وأخذوه لهذا

ASAD-NOTES:28:8#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:8#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:8#n9/r1.claim: The Pharaoh's household that found Moses was Pharaoh's own wife, as the next verse and 66:11 indicate.
ASAD-NOTES:28:8#n9/r1.anchor: As is evident from the next verse as well as from 66: 1], it was Pharaoh's own wife.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read حُزنا with ḍamma on ح; the remaining readers use fatḥa on both ح and ز.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وحزنا) بضم الحاء، وقرأ الباقون وحزنا بفتحتين .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r2.claim: حُزن and حَزَن are two regular dialect forms with the same meaning, like العجم/العجم and العرب/العرب.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p412/r2.anchor: الحزن والحزن: لغتان مثل: العجم والعجم، والعرب والعرب، وهما مطردان في هذا النحو.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy in حزن; the others use fatḥa on both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r2.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائى ﴿ وحزنا ﴾ بضم الحاء وتسكين الزاى وقرأ الباقون

NASHR:v1p223/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p223/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p223/r4.claim: Wāw should retain its clear sound when vowelled or repeated, and reciters should avoid chewing it in geminated examples such as aduwwan wa-hazanan.
NASHR:v1p223/r4.anchor: الواو: فإذا كانت مضمومة، أو مكسورة تحفظ في بيانها من أن يخالطها لفظ غيرها

NASHR:v2p341/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p341/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p341/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read ḥuznan with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy; the others fatḥ both letters.
NASHR:v2p341/r3.anchor: وحزنا فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بضم الحاء، وإسكان الزاي

QIRAAT-ER:28:8:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:11#1/r1.claim: The ḥuzn form shifts the vowel pattern from ḥazan to another attested maṣdar pattern; both mean grief or sorrow, reflecting dialectal morphology.
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:11#1/r1.anchor: Both ḥazan and ḥuzn are attested gerunds of h-z-n with essentially identical meaning

QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r1.claim: The canonical ten-reader form drops hamza from khāṭiʾīn with vowel compensation; the dominant analysis keeps the sense sinners.
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r1.anchor: Hamza-drop variant: khāṭiʾīn → khāṭīn, elision of the hamza with vowel compensation. Canonical within the ten readings.

QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r2.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r2.speaker: some grammarians
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r2.claim: Some grammarians suggest a possible derivation from khaṭā, to step or walk, yielding those who tread; the source says the dominant reading remains a pronunciation variant meaning sinners.
QIRAAT-ER:28:8:19#1/r2.anchor: Some grammarians note this could theoretically derive from a different root (khaṭā ""to step, walk"") meaning

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r1.claim: The opening fāʾ is explicative of an omitted sequence: the mother nursed him and cast him into the river as commanded, with the deletion conveying how promptly she obeyed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r1.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى : ( فالتقطه آل فرعون ( فصيحة والتقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r2.claim: A midwife summoned at Moses' birth saw light between his eyes, felt her limbs tremble and love for him, and urged his mother to hide him; when Pharaoh's agents searched, his mother hid him in a blazing oven, where God made the fire cool and safe.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r2.anchor: لما ضربها الطلق دعت قابلة من الموكلات بحبالى بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r3.claim: After nursing him for three, four, or eight months according to differing reports, his mother feared discovery and made a reed chest coated inside with pitch.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r3.anchor: وأرضعته ثلاثة أشهر أو أربعة أو ثمانية على اختلاف الروايات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r4.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says she had a carpenter make a chest with its lock inside and set Moses in the Nile near Pharaoh's house; Asiya's bathing attendants found it, mistook it for treasure, and brought the child to her.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r4.anchor: وعن السدي أنها دعت نجارا فصنع لها تابوتا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r5.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r5.claim: Asiya loved Moses and persuaded Pharaoh to spare him when he wanted to kill him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r5.anchor: وأراد فرعون قتله فلم تزل تكلمه حتى تركه لها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r6.claim: A report says Pharaoh's only child, a daughter afflicted with severe leprosy, was told that the saliva of a human-like being found at the Nile on a certain sunrise would cure her; she rubbed Moses' saliva on her skin and recovered.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p45#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وغيره أنه كان لفرعون يومئذ بنت

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r1.claim: One continuation says the girl was cured merely by seeing Moses' face; Pharaoh's advisers suspected he was the feared child, but Asiya asked Pharaoh to give him to her and he relented.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r1.anchor: وقيل : لما نظرت إلى وجهه برأت فقالت الغواة من قوم فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r2.claim: Āl Firʿawn means Pharaoh's followers; restricting āl to people of noble standing reflects the usual case, or a broader honor that includes both real and outward rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r2.anchor: وآل فرعون أتباعه وقولهم : إن الآل لايستعمل إلا فيما فيه شرف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r3.claim: Their taking him is like picking up a lost object: they deliberately cared for him and protected him from being lost.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r3.anchor: أخذ اللقطة أي أخذ اعتناء به وصيانة له عن الضياع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r4.claim: One analysis treats his becoming an enemy and grief as if it were the remote purpose of adoption and benefit, leaving the comparison implicit while the lām retains its literal purposive sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r4.anchor: الأول أن يشبه كونه كدوا وحزنا بالعلة الغائبة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r5.speaker: السكاكي والتفتازاني
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r5.claim: Al-Sakkākī, followed by al-Taftāzānī, first compare the arrangement of non-final and final purposes, then use the lām metaphorically for the resulting arrangement; the trope is primary in causality and derivative in the particle.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r5.anchor: كما ذهب إليه السكاكي وتبعه العلامة التفتازاني

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r6.speaker: الخطيب الدمشقي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r6.claim: Al-Khaṭīb al-Dimashqī's analysis first compares Moses' being their enemy and grief with a final purpose, then transfers that comparison to the relation expressed by the lām, without a trope in its genitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r6.anchor: ما أفاده كلام الخطيب الدمشقي في التلخيص والايضاح

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r7.speaker: العلامة عبد الحكيم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm calls al-Khaṭīb's analysis correct: since the lām's meaning depends on its genitive, its figurative transfer should follow the comparison applied to that genitive, not an abstract comparison of meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r7.anchor: واختار ذلك العلامة عبد الحكيم فقال : وهو الحق عندي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r8.claim: The objection that picking something up is involuntary and so cannot have a purpose is mistaken: the purpose belongs to their deliberate taking and care of what they found.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r8.anchor: واستشكل أصل تعليل الالتقاط بأن الالتقاط الوجدان من غير قصد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r9.claim: Some attach the lām to an implied “He decreed the taking so that…,” but al-Ālūsī dismisses this as an unsuitable supposition about God's speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم يحتمل تعلق اللام بمقدار أي قدرنا الالتقاط ليكون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r10.claim: Calling Moses himself grief is an emphatic exaggeration.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r10.anchor: وفي جعله عليه السلام نفس الحزن مالا يخفى من المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r11.speaker: ابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وابن سعدان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r11.claim: Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Saʿdān read ḥuznan with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وابن سعدان حزنا بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r12.speaker: جمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v20p46/r12.claim: The majority read ḥazanan with both the ḥāʾ and zāy bearing fatḥa; this is the language of Quraysh.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r1.claim: They were wrong in all they did and left, or habitually erring; their killing thousands of infants and then raising Moses was no new departure from their error.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r1.anchor: في كل ما يأتون وما يذرون أو من شأنهم الخطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r2.claim: A report says ninety thousand newborn boys were slaughtered while Pharaoh's people searched for Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r2.anchor: وروي أنه ذبح في طلبه عليه السلام تسعون ألف وليد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r3.claim: Khāṭiʾīn may derive from error in judgment, or from khaṭiʾa, to sin deliberately; on the latter reading it means sinners, whom God punished by having their enemy raised in their own care.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من خطيء بمعنى أذنب وفي الاساس يقال : خطيء خطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r4.claim: If it means error, the closing clause is parenthetical and reinforces the error already implied by the ironic claim that they raised an enemy and grief; if it means sin, it reinforces their guilt.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r4.anchor: والجملة على الأول اعتراض بين المتعاطفين لتأكيد خطئهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r5.claim: On the sin interpretation, some say the clause must be parenthetical to explain the cause of their affliction; if that affliction means Moses becoming their enemy and grief, it may also be an explanatory resumption.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r5.anchor: وقيل : يتعين عليه أن تكون اعتراضا لبيان الموجب لما ابتلوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r6.speaker: قُرِئَ
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r6.claim: A non-hamzated reading is most plausibly the same word with its hamza dropped; another suggestion derives it from khaṭā, to step, figuratively missing the right course.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p47/r6.anchor: وقريء خاطئين بغير همز فاحتمل أن يكون أصله الهمز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p193/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p193/r1.speaker: آسية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p193/r1.claim: The account says Āsiya named the child Mūsā because they found him among water and trees, glossing the name’s parts as water and tree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p193/r1.anchor: فقيل لآسية سميه فقالت: سميته موسى لأنا وجدناه في الماء والشجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r4.claim: The clause about his becoming their enemy and grief explains the outcome of their taking him, presented as though it were their motive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r4.anchor: تعليل لالتقاطهم إياه بما هو عاقبته ومؤداه تشبيها له بالغرض الحامل عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r6.claim: They were wrong in everything: after killing thousands to find Moses, they raised him to maturity so he could do what they feared; the sentence emphasizes their error or explains their affliction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r6.anchor: في كل شيء فليس ببدع منهم أن قتلوا ألوفا لأجله ثم أخذوه يربونه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.claim: Alternatively, they were sinners, and God punished them by having them raise their enemy themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.anchor: أو مذنبين فعاقبهم الله تعالى بأن ربى عدوهم على أيديهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.claim: A reading خاطين lightens خطئين; another has خاطين, those who make error in place of correctness.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p464/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p464/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p464/r5.claim: Pharaoh slaughtered Israelite sons to prevent the feared child’s rise, but God arranged for Moses to be born and raised in the household Pharaoh feared.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p464/r5.anchor: فأولدنا من بني إسرائيل الولد الذي كان يحذره فرعون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r10.claim: After nursing him, his mother sealed him in a waterproof, pitch-coated chest and cast it into the Nile; the current carried it near Pharaoh’s house, where a tree caught it and his people found it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r10.anchor: صنعت له صندوقا وقيرته لئلا يدخل إليه الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r11.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r11.claim: Al-Baghawī explains iltiqāṭ as finding something without having sought it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r11.anchor: قال البغوي : والالتقاط وجود الشيء من غير طلب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r12.claim: Pharaoh’s household found the chest and loved Moses because God placed love for him in their hearts, then adopted him.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p465/r13.claim: The account says they named him Moses because they found him in water and tree; mu meant water and sā tree in their language.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r1.claim: Moses would oppose them by rejecting their religion and calling them to truth, and grieve them through loss of kingdom and destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r1.anchor: أي بطول خوفهم منه بمخالفته لهم في دينهم وحملهم على الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r2.claim: Moses’ signs would destroy those God willed, kill the Egyptian firstborn and free Israel, then bring a drowning that grieved the whole region.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r2.anchor: ثم يهلك جميع أبكارهم فيخلص جميع بني إسرائيل منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r3.claim: The purpose lām is ironic: the family is said to have taken Moses for this end, though they could not knowingly adopt the child who would destroy them; the comparison likens him to a lion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r3.anchor: فهذه اللام للعلة استعيرت الأسد للشجاع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r4.claim: Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops shared one disposition, so it is unsurprising they raised the Israelite child they feared while slaughtering Israelite sons.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r5.claim: Their habit was deliberate sinning and straying from right aims, explaining their foolish treatment of Moses and false claim to divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r5.anchor: أي دابهم تعمد الذنوب , والضلال عن المقاصد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayd treats akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa as two dialect forms with the same meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : أخطأ وخطأ - لغتان بمعنى واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r7.speaker: ابن عرفة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r7.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says both expressions can describe following a mistaken path, intentionally or unintentionally.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r8.speaker: الأموي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r8.claim: Al-Amwī distinguishes someone who misses despite aiming at what is right from someone who deliberately does what ought not be done.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r8.anchor: وقال الأموي , المخطىء من أراد الصواب فصار إلى غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r9.speaker: ابن ظريف
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r9.claim: Ibn Ẓarīf glosses khaṭiʾa or akhṭaʾahu as failing to hit or attain something.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r9.anchor: وقال ابن ظريف في الأفعال : خطىء الشيء خطأ وأخطأه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r10.claim: The account briefly gives the ending before returning to Pharaoh’s household, framing the story with their error and arousing interest in its details.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p466/r10.anchor: بجمع طرفي القصة إجمالا وتشويقا إلى تفصيل ذلك الإجمال

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن الحبلي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r1.claim: Al-Hubuli reports that Pharaoh’s wife and her leprous daughter found the ark at sea; the daughter opened it, took Moses, and was cured.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن الحبلي قال : خرجت امراة فرعون إلى البحر وابنة لفرعون برصاء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r2.claim: In a letter defending God’s prior decree, ʿUmar argues Moses was destined to become Pharaoh’s enemy and sorrow; this rebuts the claim that Pharaoh could have been his supporter. He cites God’s instruction to Moses and Aaron.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r2.anchor: عمر بن عبد العزيز إلى النفر الذين كتبوا إلى بما لم يكن لهم بحق من رد كتاب الله ، وتكذيبهم باقدار الله النافذة في علمه السابق

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses became Pharaoh’s enemy in the eventual outcome, as God willed; that outcome was not why Pharaoh’s household adopted him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا قال : ليكون لهم في عاقبة امره عدوا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq describes Pharaoh as exceptionally rebellious, outspoken, and long-reigning among his people, and reports his name as al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r4.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق قال : لم يكن منهم فرعون اعتى على الله ، ولا اعظم قولا ، ولا اطول عمرا في ملكه منه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Pharaoh was a non-Arab from Hamadhān.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال : كان فرعون علجا من همذان

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Hāmān led Pharaoh’s vanguard with 1,700,000 horses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2943/r6.anchor: عن السدي قال : كان على مقدمة فرعون هامان في الف الف وسبعمائة الف حصان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r8.claim: Al-iltiqāt is the act of picking up something cast on the ground or elsewhere, whether deliberately or inadvertently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r8.anchor: افتعال من اللقط ، وهو تناول الشيء الملقى في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r9.claim: The act is attributed to Pharaoh's household because one of the women around Pharaoh's daughter retrieved Moses's chest from the Nile, as Exodus chapter 2 relates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r9.anchor: أسند الالتقاط إلى آل فرعون لأن استخراج تابوت موسى من النهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r10.claim: The lām is the preposition lām kay, governing a verbal noun understood from أن plus the subjunctive verb and ordinarily marking the agent's motivating cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r10.anchor: منسبك من ( أن ) المقدرة بعد اللام ومن الفعل المنصوب بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r11.claim: The family adopted Moses from compassion, not to make him their enemy; because enmity and grief were the outcome, the result is metaphorically phrased as the cause, a dependent metaphor according to most rhetoricians, unlike al-Sakkaki.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p74/r11.anchor: لم يكن داعيهم إلى التقاطه أن يكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to Pharaoh's ruling household as the dynasty, state, or nation; Moses became the enemy of a later Pharaoh and his regime.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r1.anchor: وضمير { لهم } يعود إلى آل فرعون باعتبار الوصف العنواني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r2.claim: Ḥuznan is a verbal noun with an omitted relation meaning grief for them; it is not a source noun used as an adjective for emphasis, and attributing grief to Moses is a causal metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r2.anchor: ووصفه بالحزن وهو مصدر على تقدير متعلق محذوف ، أي حزنا لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read ḥuzn with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and a still zāy; the form is a dialect variant like al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r3.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي وهما لغتان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r4.claim: Their criminality explains God's making Moses their enemy and grief, as punishment for oppressing the Israelites and worshipping idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r4.anchor: أي قدر الله نجاة موسى ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا ، لأنهم كانوا مجرمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r5.claim: Khāṭiʾ is the active participle of khaṭiʾa, to commit a sin; its verbal noun is khaṭʾ, distinct from khaṭaʾ, which means unintentional error and comes from أخطأ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r5.anchor: اسم فاعل من خطىء كفرح إذا فعل الخطيئة وهي الإثم والذنب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r6.speaker: نفطويه والجوهري والحريري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r6.claim: Nuftawayh, followed by al-Jawhari and al-Hariri, distinguishes خطئ for committing sin from أخطأ for making an error, reflecting separate usage by eloquent speakers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r6.anchor: وعلى التفرقة بين أخطأ وخطىء درج نفطويه وتبعه الجوهري والحريري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd and Ibn Qutayba instead treat the two forms as synonyms or dialect variants; al-Zamakhshari's explanation here appears to follow them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p76/r7.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة إلى أن اللفظين مترادفان وأنهما لغتان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r1.claim: Picking up means finding or taking something without having sought it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r1.anchor: الالتقاط إصابة الشئ من غير طلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh's female attendants took the ark from the water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r2.anchor: أحدها جواري امرأة فرعون قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r3.speaker: محمد بن قيس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays says Pharaoh's daughter took the ark.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r3.anchor: والثاني ابنة فرعون قاله محمد بن قيس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Pharaoh's agents took the ark.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r4.anchor: والثالث أعوان فرعون قاله ابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r5.claim: This is the lām of consequence: the outcome was that Moses became their enemy, not why they took him; the explanation was given in Yunus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r5.anchor: أي ليصير بهم الأمر إلى ذلك لا أنهم أخذوه لهذا وهذه اللام تسمى لام العاقبة وقد شرحناه في يونس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r6.claim: One view makes Moses an enemy to their religion and a grief because of what he did to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r6.anchor: أحدهما ليكون لهم عدوا في دينهم وحزنا لما يصنعه بهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r7.claim: Another view makes him an enemy to their men and grief for their women: men were drowned and women enslaved.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p203/r7.anchor: والثاني عدو لرجالهم وحزنا على نسائهم فقتل الرجال بالغرق واستعبد النساء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r1.claim: The Copts feared that killing Israelite boys would eventually leave them without laborers for their arduous work, so they warned Pharaoh that the elders would die and women could not replace men.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r1.anchor: إنه يوشك -إن استمر هذا الحال -أن يموت شيوخهم، وغلمانهم لا يعيشون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r2.claim: Pharaoh ordered newborn boys killed in alternating years; Aaron was born in a spared year, while Moses was born in a killing year.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r2.anchor: فأمر بقتل الولدان عاما وتركهم عاما، فولد هارون، عليه السلام، في السنة التي يتركون فيها الولدان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r3.claim: Pharaoh appointed watchers and midwives to register pregnancies and inspect births; Coptic women alone attended Israelite mothers at delivery.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r3.anchor: وكان لفرعون أناس موكلون بذلك، وقوابل يدرن على النساء، فمن رأينها قد حملت أحصوا اسمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r4.claim: If a woman gave birth to a girl, the attendants left her; if she bore a boy, armed executioners entered and killed him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r4.anchor: فإذا ولدت المرأة جارية تركنها وذهبن، وإن ولدت غلاما دخل أولئك الذباحون، بأيديهم الشفار المرهفة، فقتلوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r5.claim: Moses' pregnancy showed no usual signs and escaped the midwives' notice; after his birth his mother feared for and dearly loved him, and people who saw him loved him too. Ibn Kathir links this to God placing love on him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r5.anchor: لم يظهر عليها مخايل الحمل كغيرها، ولم تفطن لها الدايات، ولكن لما وضعته ذكرا ضاقت به ذرعا، وخافت عليه خوفا شديدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r8.claim: One day she put Moses in the basket when a feared visitor arrived, forgot to tie it, and the river carried it to Pharaoh's house.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r8.anchor: وأرسلته في البحر وذهلت عن أن تربطه، فذهب مع الماء واحتمله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r9.claim: Pharaoh's maidservants found the basket and brought it to his wife without knowing its contents; she opened it, saw a beautiful boy, and God placed love for him in her heart, to her good fortune and her husband's ruin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p221/r9.anchor: فالتقطه الجواري فاحتملنه، فذهبن به إلى امرأة فرعون، ولا يدرين ما فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others take the lām as indicating an eventual consequence, not the family's purpose, since they did not intend to capture someone who would become their enemy and grief.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r2.claim: Although the wording appears to support Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Kathir prefers a purposive lām in light of the context: God caused them to take Moses so he would become their enemy and grief, more fully defeating their precautions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r2.anchor: ولكن إذا نظر إلى معنى السياق فإنه تبقى (5) اللام للتعليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r3.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r3.claim: In a letter to Qadariyya denying scripture and God's decrees, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz argues that God's prior knowledge made Moses Pharaoh's enemy and grief, citing the promise to show Pharaoh what he feared and rejecting the claim that Pharaoh might have chosen to support Moses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p222/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن أمير المؤمنين عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كتب كتابا إلى قوم من القدرية

JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ḥuznan with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and still zāy; others use fatḥa on both. Both are lexical variants.
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: حزنا بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي، الباقون بفتحهما، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r8.claim: Iltiqāṭ is finding something without having sought it, as with a lost object.
JISHUMI:v8p5470#2/r8.anchor: والالتقاط: إصابة الشيء من غير طلب، ومنه اللقطة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r1.claim: The لام in ليكون is the purposive لام كي, expressing cause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r1.anchor: اللام في { ليكون } هي لام كي التي معناها التعليل ، كقولك : جئتك لتكرمني سواء بسواء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r2.claim: The causality is metaphorical: Pharaoh's family picked Moses up from affection and adoption, but the result is presented as though it motivated the act.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r2.anchor: ولكن معنى التعليل فيها وارد على طريق المجاز دون الحقيقة ، لأنه لم يكن داعيهم إلى الالتقاط أن يكون لهم عدوا وحزنا ، ولكن : المحبة والتبني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r3.claim: The metaphor is like presenting an outcome as a cause, as in coming “to honor me” or striking someone “so he may be disciplined.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r3.anchor: غير أن ذلك لما كان نتيجة التقاطهم له وثمرته ، شبه بالداعي الذي يفعل الفاعل الفعل لأجله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r4.claim: حزنا and حُزنا are two language forms, like العدم and العدم.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r4.anchor: وقرىء : ( وحزنا ) وهما لغتان : كالعدم والعدم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r5.claim: خاطئين may mean Pharaoh's people were wrong in everything, so raising their enemy was typical of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r5.anchor: { كانوا خاطئين } في كل شيء ، فليس خطؤهم في تربية عدوهم ببدع منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r6.claim: Alternatively, they were criminals whom God punished by making them raise their own enemy and destroyer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r6.anchor: أو كانوا مذنبين مجرمين ، فعاقبهم الله بأن ربي عدوهم ومن هو سبب هلاكهم على أيديهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r7.claim: A reading has خاطين, either a shortened form of خاطئين or meaning those who strayed from right into error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p398/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( خاطين ) ، تخفيف خاطئين ، أو خاطين الصواب إلى الخطأ .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Pharaoh's wife's attendants found the infant's chest when they went out to draw water and carried it to her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنه التقطه جواري امرأته حين خرجن لاستسقاء الماء فوجدن تابوته فحملنه إليها , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says Pharaoh's wife, who had leprosy, found the chest at the sea, took the infant, and was cured; she called him blessed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن امرأة فرعون خرجت إلى البحر وكانت برصاء فوجدت تابوته فأخذته فبرئت من برصها فقالت : هذا الصبي مبارك , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r4.claim: The verse names the eventual outcome as if it were already present: Moses was not then an enemy or grief, since Pharaoh's wife rejoiced in and deeply loved him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r4.anchor: في عاقبة أمره ولم يكن لهم في الحال عدوا ولا حزنا لأن امرأة فرعون فرحت به وأحبته حبا شديدا فذكر الحال بالمآل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r5.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r5.claim: The cited anonymous poetic line about death nurturing every nursing mother illustrates naming a present state by its eventual outcome.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p236/r5.anchor: كما قال الشاعر : وللمنايا تربي كل مرضعة ودورنا لخراب الدهر نبنيها .

MUQATIL:28:8-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s household found Moses in his chest among water and trees; Muqatil derives his name from Coptic mo (water) and si (tree).
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r1.anchor: من البحر من بين الماء والشجر، وهو في التابوت

MUQATIL:28:8-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r2.claim: Moses would be their enemy through their destruction and a source of grief and anger over the killing of their firstborn; linked to 26:55.
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r2.anchor: { ليكون لهم عدوا } في الهلاك { وحزنا } يعني وغيظا في قتل الأبكار

MUQATIL:28:8-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r3.claim: Muqatil repeats the verse’s judgment that Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops were wrongdoers.
MUQATIL:28:8-11/r3.anchor: { إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r1.claim: Al-taqaṭahu means that Pharaoh's people took the child.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r1.anchor: أخذه قال الزجاج كان فرعون من أهل فارس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Pharaoh was Persian, from Istakhr.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج كان فرعون من أهل فارس من اصطخر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the outcome as the sense: they did not take Moses in order to make him their enemy; events came to that end, as in the saying about a child being born for death.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r3.anchor: قاله الزجاج وعن هذا قال المفسرون ان هذه لام العاقبة والصيرورة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r4.speaker: المفسرون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r4.claim: The commentators call the lām the lām of consequence or eventual outcome.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون ان هذه لام العاقبة والصيرورة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r5.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf calls it a purpose lām, but says its causal sense is figurative because the outcome of their taking him resembles a motive for it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r5.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشاف هي لام كي التي معناها التعليل كقولك جئتك لتكرمني ولكن معنى التعليل فيها وارد على طريق المجاز

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r6.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r6.claim: Hamza reads the alternate form ḥuzn; both forms are Arabic variants, like the two forms of ʿadam.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r6.anchor: وحزنا على حمزة وهما لغتان كالعدم والعدم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar lightens the hamza in the reading of khāṭiʾīn.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r8.claim: They were sinners, and God punished them by raising their enemy and eventual destroyer in their own household; their wrongdoing in everything made this outcome typical of them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p227#3/r8.anchor: أي كانوا مذنبين فعاقبهم الله بان ربي عدوهم ومن هو سبب هلاكهم على أيديهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.claim: The lām marks consequence, not the family's intention: they took Moses hoping for joy, but the outcome was that he became their enemy and grief.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r7.anchor: فاللام في { ليكون } لام العاقبة ولام الصيرورة لأنهم إنما أخذوه ليكون لهم قرة عين

QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates the consequence construction by saying that every nursing mother nurtures someone destined for death and every home is built for ruin.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r8.anchor: وللمنايا تربي كل مرضعة ودورنا لخراب الدهر نبنيها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r9.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r9.claim: A second unnamed poet likewise says mothers raise children for death and houses are built for destruction, demonstrating outcome rather than intent.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r9.anchor: فللموت تغدو الوالدات سخالها كما لخراب الدهر تبنى المساكن

QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r10.claim: التقاط is finding something without seeking or intending it; Arabic also uses the verb for an accidental encounter, and the legal discussion of found property was treated in Surat Yusuf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:7-8/r10.anchor: والالتقاط وجود الشيء من غير طلب ولا إرادة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r1.claim: The poetic phrase منهلا وردته التقاطا illustrates an accidental finding; the word is also the source of luqata, lost property, whose rules were discussed in Surat Yusuf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r1.anchor: ومنهل وردته التقاطا ومنه اللقطة. وقد مضى بيان ذلك من الأحكام

QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r2.speaker: الأعمش ويحيى والمفضل وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r2.claim: These readers pronounce حزنًا with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and sukūn on zāy; the remaining readers use fatḥa on both, which Abu ʿUbayd selects, and Abu Hatim favors emphatic pronunciation.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى والمفضل وحمزة والكسائي وخلف: { وحزنا } بضم الحاء وسكون الزاي

QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r3.claim: The two pronunciations are dialectal forms, like the variant pairs for want, sickness, and right guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r3.anchor: وهما لغتان مثل العدم والعدم، والسقم والسقم، والرشد والرشد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r4.claim: Haman was Pharaoh's minister and was a Copt.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:8-9/r5.claim: The verse calls Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops disobedient, polytheistic sinners.
